source.title: Gradient Ascent Post-training Enhances Language Model Generalization
source.authors: Dongkeun Yoon; Joel Jang; Sungdong Kim; Minjoon Seo

record.file_problem: The supplied text appears to contain the full paper, including appendices and tables.
record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates how a different training intervention, gradient-ascent post-training, affects held-out downstream-task performance in pretrained language models. It does not test the listed versions’ random-label memorization, architecture, optimizer, batch-size, regularization, or sharpness claims.
record.gate_note: The paper reports held-out task scores after GAP, but does not measure training error, train-test gaps, or random-label fitting. Results below are recorded as findings about generalization performance outside the listed versions; cited prior work is not extracted as this study’s result.
record.test_reason: The study evaluates gradient-ascent post-training on pretrained OPT models, without testing any V1–V8 comparison. Its background discussion of sharp minima supplies no measurement of magnitude-aware sharpness or generalization gaps. Improved downstream scores alone do not test these versions.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially correct. The authors present GAP as a promising way to improve downstream performance, especially dialogue generation, and report the most reliable dialogue gains from unfamiliar Github text. Classification improvements are inconsistent. Although no task-specific fine-tuning data are used, task validation data are required for checkpoint selection; sample selection and scaling beyond 300 runs per model size remain future work.
record.recipe_differences: Unsupervised gradient ascent post-training on random unlabeled text; evaluation is on pretrained OPT language models and downstream NLP tasks, not the listed random-label/generalization-gap experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary by task and model size; the paper reports inconsistent classification-task improvement and more reliable dialogue gains from Github text.

fits_no_version.finding: Selected GAP checkpoints improve dialogue test F1 over same-size OPT baselines in all 12 Table 7 comparisons.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A few gradient-ascent updates on unlabeled text can improve dialogue test F1 for pretrained OPT models when checkpoints are selected using task validation data.

record.peer_reviewed: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
record.problems: The paper selects the best-performing checkpoint using validation data; only 300 GAP runs per model size are reported. The supplied text gives no uncertainty estimates for the Table 7 test scores. GAP performance on classification tasks is inconsistent, and the paper says selecting suitable text samples remains future work.
record.rows_left_out: Table 1 reports aggregate test metrics across dialogue datasets, and Tables 8–10 report other dialogue test metrics; these are omitted because the extracted per-dataset F1 rows already capture the held-out performance outcome. Validation results in Tables 5–6 and human preference results in Table 2 are omitted because they are not the dialogue test F1 scores recorded here.

untested.parts: Coexistence of random-label fitting capacity and natural-label generalization, including chance performance on held-out random labels.
Width-dependent test error beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization and the role of local connectivity or initialization.
Adaptive versus SGD optimization and sensitivity to tuning, weight decay, or switching optimizers.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adapted training recipes.
Effects of adding or removing dropout and weight decay across data regimes.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, its association with generalization gaps, and comparison with norm- or margin-based measures.
Retraining after removing highly memorized versus equally many random training examples.

record.verdict_notes: Using Adam without dropout or weight decay does not test V4 or V6 because neither factor is compared. Corpus familiarity is assumed rather than established through OPT memorization measurements; GAP does not remove examples and retrain as V8 requires. The cannot_determine states concern the listed versions, not the readable direction of the F1 improvements.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance on natural versus random labels.
Width beyond interpolation and its effect on test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected architecture and local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD and the effects of tuning, weight decay, or optimizer switching.
Large versus small batch training under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Dropout and weight-decay effects on held-out error.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and other measured properties as predictors of train-test gap.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring the resulting test accuracy.

rows.subject: OPT 350M + GAP
rows.operation_detail: Gradient Ascent Post-training on one random unlabeled text sample for up to 15 steps; best validation checkpoint evaluated on dialogue test sets.
rows.note: Paired values are given as OPT baseline followed by + GAP.
rows.check: Values match Table 7; this is the proposed method's performance comparison, outside V1–V8. Checkpoint selection also excludes outliers.
